scope.flow: FastAccessVault rebalanceFunds() pushes excess liquidity to Custodian, enabling repeated draining of fast-access buffer
scope.environment: on-chain FastAccessVault with off-chain Custodian replenishment

statements.text: The vault exposes a public/external rebalanceFunds()-style function with no caller restriction.
The rebalanceFunds() function has no rate-limit/cooldown, no minimum amount threshold, and no upper bound preventing the Vault from being drained to the target level.
The vault balance exceeds the target so that excess = vaultBalance - target is nonzero.
Incoming top-ups from the Custodian are handled off-chain and may be slow.
Attacker immediately calls rebalanceFunds() after each mint to push the freshly created excess off-chain to the Custodian.
Attacker repeats the rebalanceFunds() calls continually at low gas cost per call.
rebalanceFunds() computes excess = vaultBalance - target and immediately transfers excess to the Custodian on-chain, with no caller restriction, rate-limit, minimum threshold, or upper bound.
The Vault should retain sufficient fast-access liquidity so that legitimate large redeems can be satisfied without waiting for off-chain Custodian top-ups.
The rebalanceFunds() operation should not allow an unprivileged caller to repeatedly drain the Vault buffer to the bare target level.

ambiguities: Report does not state a concrete prior vault balance or target value establishing excess before the action; excess is computed by the action itself.
Report does not specify whether the attacker must first perform a mint or only monitor existing mints.
No explicit numeric rate-limit, cooldown, or threshold values are given.
Whether the attacker is truly unprivileged is stated only as 'no privileged access' in impact text, not as a precondition.
